artworks.title: Cerulean Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds on a branch with red berries and leaves. The birds are primarily blue with white and black accents, perched on a branch against a cream-colored background.

artworks.title: Blue-green Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a blue-green bird perched on a branch of a plant with clusters of pink berries. The image features a bird sitting upon a branch with leaves and pink berries. The bird has blue plumage with black-and-white markings. The plant is labeled as "Spanish Mulberry." The background is simple to emphasize the details of the bird and plant. The illustration showcases precision in depicting the bird and foliage in a botanical style.

artworks.title: Swainson's Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Swainson's Warbler perched on a branch with large green leaves and acorns. The painting depicts a small bird with a blend of gray, yellow, and black plumage, showcasing the intricate details of its feathers, particularly the white and black pattern along its wings. The branch it is perched on extends diagonally across the canvas, with large, textured leaves of a vibrant green hue. Nestled among the leaves are a few clustered acorns. The overall composition highlights the bird’s stance and the botanical features with attention to detail.

artworks.title: Red Tailed Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two hawks in combat over a hare. The upper hawk has vibrant red tail feathers and intricate patterns of brown, black, and white on its wings, displaying a sense of intense motion and aggression. The lower hawk lies across, its body and wings horizontal, adding tension and drama to the composition. The hare appears lifeless, with a notable detail of red staining near its midsection, indicating a struggle. In the background, a faint outline of distant mountains can be seen. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Chuck Will's Widow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds and a snake interacting on a branch. The birds have elaborately patterned feathers and are perched on a branch alongside a vibrantly colored snake. The snake has black, red, and yellow bands and appears to be slithering along the branch. There are green leaves and bright pink buds surrounding the birds and snake. The painting combines a naturalistic portrayal of the wildlife subjects with a focus on detailed textures and colors.

artworks.title: Painted Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting depicts colorful birds, called "Fringilla Ciris" or Painted Buntings, on a branch. The birds have vibrant plumage in shades of blue, red, and green, set against a plain background. They are shown in various poses on a leafy branch with green berries, including one bird holding a thread in its beak. The style of the painting is reminiscent of the detailed realism of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Rice Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on branches with hanging red seeds. The painting features a black and white bird with intricate brown patterning on its wings and a pale orange patch around its neck standing atop a branch adorned with vibrant red, maple-like samaras. Below, another smaller bird with an olive and beige plumage appears poised as if about to leap from another branch. The branches are sparsely filled with clusters of winged seeds cascading downward, offering a splash of vivid color against the subdued backdrop.

artworks.title: Cuvier's Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A small bird with a red crown and intricate markings on its wings is perched on the branch of a flowering plant. The plant features large green leaves and clusters of pink flowers with star-shaped patterns. The background is a pale, light cream color. The bird is perched on a horizontal branch, surrounded by leaves and flowers both above and below it. The illustration's title and scientific labels are located in the lower right corner.

artworks.title: Red-shouldered Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two red-shouldered hawks perched on a branch. The hawks are detailed, showing patterns on their feathers in shades of brown, red, and grey. They have sharp beaks and intense eyes. The background is plain, emphasizing the birds' colorful feathers. Branches with leaves and a vine are depicted. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Loggerhead Shrike
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a vine-entangled branch with a small rodent. The image features two birds with black and white plumage engaging with one another while perched on a twisting branch covered in vines and green leaves. On the right side of the branch, a small rodent is depicted hanging by its tail. The background is a plain, muted tone, which enhances the details and color of the flora and fauna. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed representations of birds.

artworks.title: Hermit Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Hermit Thrushes perched on a branch with berries. The artwork features two detailed and realistic Hermit Thrush birds positioned on a bare branch adorned with clusters of red and orange berries. The birds are depicted in a naturalistic style, showcasing fine feather details and the characteristic markings of Hermit Thrushes. The branches are rendered in subtle grays and browns, contributing to the overall muted color palette of the painting. The composition captures a serene encounter in nature, with a small insect and a green worm adorning the space around the birds.

artworks.title: Chestnut-sided Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two chestnut-sided warblers are perched on a flowering plant with pink blossoms. The birds have rich chestnut and yellow hues, contrasting with the green foliage and soft pink flowers. The birds are positioned along the vertical stem of the plant, with one bird higher up facing right, and the other slightly lower, angled to the left. Pink flowers and green leaves are scattered around the birds, creating a naturalistic composition.

artworks.title: Carbonated Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on branches with green leaves and red berries.

artworks.title: Great Horned Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two great horned owls perched on a branch. Two owls are depicted in intricate detail, one taller than the other, situated on a branch. The owls have yellow eyes and ear tufts, with detailed feathers in brown, black, and white. The branch is realistically depicted, with subtle details like moss or lichen. The background is neutral, highlighting the owls' features. The style resembles that of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Passenger Pigeon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: In this print, two pigeons are perched on tree branches. One pigeon is perched above the other and bends its head downward. The bird on the bottom lifts its head up to meet the higher bird. The birds are interacting, with the closed beak of the higher bird inside the open beak of the lower bird. The pigeon on the bottom has a reddish breast, a sky-blue head and body, and blue wings with black and gray tips, and it stands on a dark a branch covered in light blue lichen. The other pigeon has earth-toned brown and soft blue plumage with black markings, and it perches on a lighter brown branch with light red lichen. Dried brown leaves hang from the upper branch, and the background is plain paper.

artworks.title: White-eyed Fly Catcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched on a branch, with pink flowers and green leaves surrounding it. The bird is depicted with a yellow eye-ring and brown and white plumage. The branch it is perched upon is slender and graceful, with clusters of pink flowers. The green leaves are lush and intricately veined, cascading down the painting. To the right of the bird, there is a small, flying insect with striped details. Soft pastel colors are used for the flowers, contrasting with the vivid colors of the bird.

artworks.title: Swamp Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a small bird on a branch surrounded by large, leafy foliage and a single white flower nearby. The color palette consists of natural greens from the leaves, browns from the bird, and white from the flower.

artworks.title: Rathbone Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two yellow birds perched among flowers and leaves. The painting shows two yellow birds on a vine with red and yellow flowers. The plant elements are depicted realistically against a white background, creating a harmonious composition.

artworks.title: Ivory-billed Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James

artworks.title: Red-winged Starling
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of red-winged blackbirds among blooming tree branches. Three birds perch on separate branches, showcasing shades of brown, black, and hints of red. A fourth bird is depicted in flight with its wings spread wide, displaying its red wing patches against a dark body. The branches have small pink blossoms. The style is similar to John James Audubon, with detailed renderings of birds in their natural environment. The composition highlights the beauty of the birds in a serene setting, focusing on ornithological accuracy.

artworks.title: Republican Cliff Swallow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of several cliff swallows and their nests on a rocky surface. The image features three swallows and a cluster of intricate, tube-like nests made from mud on a rock face. The nests have openings. The rock surface shows brown hues and textures. The style is similar to John James Audubon's detailed and realistic portrayals of birds and their habitats.

artworks.title: Bay-breasted Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds perched on branches of a cotton plant with green leaves and pink flowers. The birds have orange-brown and black plumage with white accents. The dominant colors are green for the leaves, pink for the flowers, and earthy tones for the birds. The bird at the top is on the left side of the main stem, facing right, while the bird at the bottom is on the lower right, also facing right. Pink blossoms are visible on the upper and right branches of the plant.

artworks.title: Henslow's Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a bird with speckled brown, white, and black feathers perched on a moss-covered log surrounded by lush greenery and colorful flowers. The color palette consists of earthy tones of brown and green with pops of red and pink from the flowers. The bird is positioned at the center of the log, with various green leaves and a tall red flowering plant in the background. Additional pink flowers are visible to the left of the bird.

artworks.title: Winter Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a hawk capturing a frog amidst tall grasses. The hawk has its wings spread wide and beak open while seizing the frog with its talons. The bird's plumage is detailed, with a mix of browns, whites, and blacks. The tall grasses in the background add to the natural setting. The painting captures a moment of drama in the wildlife.
